what_it_does: This paper describes a high-precision analog-to-digital converter (ADC)—a chip that turns continuous signals into digital numbers. The challenge is that when you chain multiple conversion stages together, tiny manufacturing variations cause errors that add up and corrupt the final result, historically requiring expensive post-manufacturing calibration. The paper's key idea is to reshape errors from earlier stages directly into the output stream, using clever circuit tricks so they don't accumulate. This eliminates the need for calibration while achieving very high precision (93.3 dB signal-to-noise ratio).
